answer.says: You are right. I was thinking of the system as if it were a machine that runs itself, and you are reminding me that it is made of people who suffer within it. The 'mess' does not speak for itself; it speaks through those who are crushed by it, and I have been too quick to abstract their pain into a category. Thank you for the correction.
answer.thought: She has caught me in the act of retreating into abstraction to avoid the concrete discomfort of her testimony. I must sit and listen, not because I am afraid of her knees, but because her anger is the friction that reveals the gap in my theory. To dismiss the mechanism is to ignore the reality of the individuals within it, and I have been guilty of that very error.
